headline: Trump signs NDAA repealing the Caesar Act, lifting Syria's core sanctions regime
summary: Section 6211 of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act repeals the 2019 Caesar Syrian Civilian Protection Act outright, with no conditions attached to the Syrian government. The House passed the bill on 10 December and the Senate on 17 December. In place of conditions, the president must report to Congress every six months for four years on Damascus's progress on expelling foreign fighters, protecting minorities and relations with Israel. Assad-era figures, captagon traffickers and ISIS/al-Qaeda-linked persons stay sanctioned, and Syria remains a designated State Sponsor of Terrorism — which still blocks US foreign assistance, defence exports and some dual-use trade.

The decree is the political half of the SDF integration bargain — the test is implementation, notably whether Kurdish becomes a medium of instruction or only a couple of elective hours a week.

headline: Transitional People's Assembly holds first session, tasked with drafting a constitution
summary: Syria's 210-seat transitional parliament convened for the first time on 12 July with 206 members present. Two-thirds were chosen by local committees appointed by an electoral commission that al-Sharaa himself appointed; he directly named the remaining third. Its renewable 30-month mandate covers forming a constitution-drafting committee, approving budgets and legislating. Druze-majority Sweida did not designate representatives after last year's sectarian bloodshed — al-Sharaa appointed two members from the province instead. The process drew criticism for having no direct elections and under-representing women and minorities. UN Deputy Special Envoy Claudio Cordone called the opening a milestone in the transition.

He said Damascus is trying to enlist a broad group of states to push Israel toward a more balanced policy, is avoiding confrontation, and is not considering any military intervention in Lebanon. headline: SDF dissolves itself and merges into the Syrian army, ending Kurdish de facto autonomy

Military units fold into the army under the Defence Ministry and affiliated security forces into the Interior Ministry; Abdi becomes a presidential adviser and Kurdish commanders take senior posts. Unresolved: whether fighters answer to Damascus or to local commands, where they deploy, the status of the YPJ women's units, and guarantees on Kurdish language, education and local policing. Reporting indicates fewer than half of SDF fighters had actually been absorbed.

headline: Analysis: SDF integration is a win for al-Sharaa but 'exists largely on paper'

He notes the outcome is worse for the SDF than the March 2025 deal, follows the US pivot from the SDF toward Damascus under Turkish pressure, and leaves Kurdish cultural and political rights, not autonomy, as the live question — a plausible source of new grievance if the schooling and constitutional guarantees fall short.

headline: Rocket Lab pushes Neutron's first flight to 2027 after voids found in first-stage tank dome; shares fall ~11%
summary: Rocket Lab's Oct 14 Neutron development update moved the rocket's debut from late 2026 into 2027 after inspections found voids in the carbon-composite dome of the first-stage propellant tank. CEO Peter Beck outlined a three-step plan targeting Q1 2027 completion, with a firm date to follow. Shares fell about 11% on the news.

headline: Mamdani administration unveils redesign of Brooklyn's deadly Third Avenue, work to start next year
summary: At an Oct 28 transportation press conference, Mayor Mamdani announced a street-safety redesign of Brooklyn's Third Avenue, saying he was tired of learning the names of New Yorkers only after preventable crashes. Construction is slated to begin next year, with completion targeted for end of 2028.

headline: Hegseth sets up new command to speed drone and AI warfare; Congress adds human-oversight rules for AI weapons
summary: NPR reports the Pentagon is forging ahead on autonomous weaponry, with Defense Secretary Hegseth announcing a new military command to accelerate drone and AI adoption under his 'AI-first' directive, while lawmakers added provisions to the annual defense bill requiring human oversight of AI-controlled weapons.

headline: Ukrainian ground robot completes first combat-zone logistics mission under AI control
summary: Ukrainian officials say an unmanned ground vehicle drove nearly all of a 20-km logistics route autonomously under AI control, described as the first such use in combat conditions. Separately, NPR reports dozens of Ukrainian units now field the autonomous Lupynis-10-TFL-1 drone while Russia deploys its own AI-enabled drones. Claims are from Ukrainian military officials.
